column1: # /execute's wording for koto's init refusals, read by scripts/koto-open.sh
# through execute-open.sh. One `<code><TAB><text>` line per code; `{var}`,
# `{error}`, `{live}` and `{stranded}` are koto's fields, substituted and never
# evaluated. A code with no line here
# prints koto's own message. A `<code>:<VAR>` line words that code for one
# variable and wins over the code's own line: the coordinated flags on a
# single-pr PLAN are unknown_var on their variables.

column2: /execute: {value} is not a valid value for {var} (allowed: {constraint}). Nothing was started.
/execute: {var} was given more than once (for --merge, pass the flag once). Nothing was started.
/execute: {var} is not an /execute setting. Nothing was started.
/execute: --store applies only to a coordinated PLAN. Nothing was started.
/execute: --coordination-pr applies only to a coordinated PLAN. Nothing was started.
/execute: --follow-up applies only to a coordinated PLAN. Nothing was started.
/execute: --remove applies only to a coordinated PLAN. Nothing was started.
/execute: --adopt-run applies only to a coordinated PLAN. Nothing was started.
/execute: {session} is already running with {var}={recorded}, not {requested}. Finish or remove that run first; nothing was changed.
/execute: {session} is a live run of a different /execute template (a single-pr and a coordinated run share the name). Finish that run first; nothing was changed.
/execute: {session} belongs to another worktree or session store. Continue it there, or remove it with `koto session cleanup {session}`; nothing was changed.

/execute: the finished run {session} is still held by the sessions around it, and work under it is still running: {live}. Nothing was started or replaced; let that work finish, or cancel it, then invoke /execute again.
/execute: the finished run {session} could not be moved aside to make room for a fresh one, so nothing was replaced: {error} Invoke /execute again to retry.
